2609.06052.title: SkillSpec: Intent-Masked Specification Reasoning for Agent Skill Correctness
2609.06052.paper_summary: Autonomous agent systems increasingly depend on reusable skill abstractions for consolidating experiential knowledge and domain expertise. These artifacts typically bundle free-form instructions with heterogeneous resources. However, ensuring their correctness remains challenging. Their failure modes transcend conventional code defects to subtle semantic inconsistencies such as intent conflicts, which manifest as silent failures masked by the underlying model. Moreover, skill correctness must be grounded in intended task boundaries and generalizability. We propose SkillSpec, a Hoare-style framework that formulates skill correctness as a specification reasoning problem. It transforms a heterogeneous skill repository into a unified graph representation that aligns descriptions, instructions and code artifacts. For each node, SkillSpec derives an ExpectSpec from the surrounding declared intent, and infers FactSpecs from encoded behavior under partially disclosed intent. An intent mask regulates access to holistic, lineage, neighborhood, and local views to balance the bias introduced by excessive context against unsupported inference caused by insufficient context. SkillSpec jointly reasons over these views to flag candidate defects, and automatically validates them in an isolated sandbox. On 515 real-world skills from SkillsBench and widely downloaded repositories, SkillSpec identified 763 manually confirmed defects across 239 skills, achieving 61.2% precision. The node-level analysis across multiple model families shows that specification reasoning is consistently reliable for code nodes, whereas plain-text nodes remain a major bottleneck. Most defects arise at the boundaries between declared intent and implementation, demonstrating that explicit specifications provide a practical foundation for skill quality assurance in real-world agent ecosystems.
2609.06052.paper_summary_zh: 自主代理系統越來越依賴可重用的技能抽象來整合經驗知識和領域專業知識。<lb/>這些工件通常將自由形式的指令與異質資源捆綁在一起。<lb/>然而，確保它們的正確性仍然具有挑戰性。<lb/>它們的失效模式超越了傳統代碼缺陷，涉及微妙的語義不一致性，例如意圖衝突，這些衝突表現為由底層模型掩蓋的靜默失敗。<lb/>此外，技能的正確性必須基於預期的任務邊界和可概括性。<lb/>我們提出了SkillSpec，一個霍爾風格的框架，將技能的正確性表述為一個規範推理問題。<lb/>它將異質技能庫轉換為統一的圖形表示，對齊描述、指令和代碼工件。<lb/>對於每個節點，SkillSpec從周圍聲明的意圖中推導出ExpectSpec，並從部分披露的意圖下的編碼行為推斷FactSpecs。<lb/>意圖掩碼調節對整體、血統、鄰域和局部視圖的訪問，以平衡過度上下文引入的偏見與由於上下文不足而導致的無法支持的推斷。<lb/>SkillSpec共同對這些視圖進行推理，以標記候選缺陷，並在隔離的沙盒中自動驗證它們。<lb/>在SkillsBench和廣泛下載的庫中的515個真實世界技能上，SkillSpec識別了239個技能中763個手動確認的缺陷，達到61.2%的精確度。<lb/>跨多個模型系列的節點級分析顯示，規範推理對於代碼節點始終可靠，而純文本節點仍然是主要瓶頸。<lb/>大多數缺陷發生在聲明的意圖和實現之間的邊界上，這表明明確的規範為真實世界代理生態系統中的技能質量保證提供了實用的基礎。
